The test image shows a tomato stem at soil level with:
- White cottony mycelium on the stem at the soil line
- Dark rounded sclerotia embedded in the white growth
- Stem bleaching/necrosis
- Plant wilting/dying above

Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Gray_Mold, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt. Now viewing one reference from each.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Tomato stem at soil line showing dense white cottony mycelium with dark rounded sclerotia embedded in it, stem bleaching/necrosis, black plastic mulch in background
- **Bugwood ID 5593845** in test image vs **5593847** in Sclerotinia reference — consecutive numbers from the same contributor/series, very strong evidence
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum): white fluffy mycelium + large dark sclerotia on stem — matches perfectly
- **Southern_Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii): produces smaller tan-brown sclerotia, not the dark ones seen here
- **Gray_Mold**: leaf/brown necrosis pattern, no match
- **Sclerotinia lab reference**: confirms white mycelium + rounded sclerotia on stems — consistent visual signature

The Bugwood image ID (5593845) is consecutive to the Sclerotinia reference image (5593847), strongly indicating they are from the same submission.
